newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bel-20 bound for glory but Barco in line of fire.
newsitem.headline: Bel-20 bound for glory but Barco in line of fire.

text.p: The Bel-20 index of leading shares was bound for higher regions but electronics firm Barco nosedived 7.4 percent and might be heading for further trouble, dealers said on Thursday.
The Bel-20 ended flat at 1,753.29 points after sentiment was somewhat shaken by Barco and steel wire and cord maker Bekaert which announced a 25-percent drop in H1 profit on Thursday.

The index was bolstered by firm bonds and dollar, U.S. PPI data which calmed inflation fears and lifted Wall Street and -- after briefly holding its breath ahead of the release of U.S. CPI on Friday -- should add fresh gains, dealers said.
Analysts said Barco, which closed down 400 francs at 5,010, fell on the its cautious 1997 profit growth forecast and dilution of EPS after the exercising of warrants in June.
Traders did not exclude further losses for Barco, which is not part of the Bel-20. One predicted further weakness when brokerages started re-rating the stock in view of the more cautious outlook.

They said the fall was sparked by large U.S. institutional investors and led to some panicking by others. "They (U.S. investors) prefer to take their profit. At these levels they're not exactly shooting themselves in the foot," one said.
"This fall was really exaggerated," one trader said. "But if they continue to offload we can fall to 4,700," he said.
But he added that Barco, which single-handedly accounted for a third of total volume of 2.77 billion in Belgian shares, had already become attractive at current levels.
Bekaert slipped one percent to 22,975 and might dip further, dealers said. But they noted that the stock had already fallen back from 25,200 francs in the past three weeks.
Oil firm Petrofina was up 0.7 percent at 10,000, profiting from the imminent reweighting of the Bel-20, effective from September 23.
"It's not really linked to higher oil prices," one trader said. "Petrofina's oil reserves are not that substantial," she added.
Oil prices hit a new post-Gulf War high on Thursday as a nervous oil market braced for another U.S. military strike against Iraq. REUTER
